steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: See? I told you it wouldn't take up too much of your time. You said a few words, and it's taken care of, simple as that.
Holding a massive teddy bear under her arm, Mess fishes out a key with the other hand and unlocks the door.
Only just now, when the two of you walked past the toy store downstairs, Mess said to the person inside, "As usual, pack up all the new arrivals and send them upstairs."
Then she scooped up the teddy bear near the counter and made her way straight for the elevator.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: Voilà! Welcome to my humble abode!
When the door opens, you are greeted with wallpaper and interior decor that exude cuteness.
The delicate tea-things, the stuffed animals on the sofa, the anvil and hammer with cartoon stickers by the fireplace...
It is more like the living room of a teenage girl than a workshop.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: Take a seat. I'll go look for the ledger.
I can ask my people to look for it.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: There's too much stuff around here. They wouldn't be able to find it. You sit tight, and don't make it harder for me by messing around with my things.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: Oh, I almost forgot... You already did.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: By the way, there's a tin of loose tea leaves on the table; help yourself.
Mess starts searching high and low for the ledger. And you, with nothing better to do, starts appraising the decor.
You own all these stuffed animals?

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: Yes. Too many, I know... But I bought them with my own money.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: I'm rich. I've got so many commissions that I won't be able to finish them all until next year.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: Why do you ask?
Nothing. It's just that this doesn't look like your style.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: Huh?!
Mess, who has been searching for the ledger with her back to you, turns her head to look at you.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: What do you mean? Because I'm a blacksmith, a Sinner, I don't deserve to have these cute little things?
That's not what I meant.
Do you like them?
You point at the big pile of stuffed animals on the sofa.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: I do, I very much do.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: Don't you think it makes you feel better to look at cute stuff?
What about forging? Do you like it?

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: Yes, I do. One thing doesn't contradict the other.
No, not at all. I'm just feeling that...

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: Ah, I know what you're trying to say.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: Weapons are for doing harm, while stuffed animals are harmless. So you can't love them both. Is this what you're thinking?

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: I'm not the one doing the harm. I just make the weapons. And I enjoy this forging process.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: Hmm, weird... It's not here either. Where did I put it...?
You look at the little anvil near the fireplace; it has been adorably decorated, much like a kid's piano with a baking finish.
So you use this thing to forge weapons?

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: Don't be ridiculous! That's a work of art, a work of art. Use your head!

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: Forging weapons makes a lot of soot and stuff. No way I'm doing it in this lovely room. I've got common sense.
Where is your workshop then?

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: Downstairs.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: My bedroom and my living room are here. This is where I keep my non-forging-related things.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: No, not here either...
You wonder if you should give some advice to Mess, who has been running around like a headless chicken.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: Uh, no, I don't think it is.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: Oh my god, oh my god, did I actually lose it? All right then... I'll go downstairs and check.
You and Mess go downstairs and into her workshop.
The workshop is a world apart from the rooms upstairs. It is dim, dirty, and messy with a blackened ceiling, the way a traditional smithy should be.
You're making weapons in an office building. No complaints?

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: Complaints, no complaints... there's no difference. I give the management office a fat check every year; they've got my back.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: ...Let me see where you're hiding, my little precious.
Mess drags a few heavy-looking treasure chests out into the open space.
She opens the lids. The chests are crammed with weapons of all kinds, but mainly frightening cold weapons of different sizes.
For some reason, you feel instinctively uncomfortable when you see them.
These are...?

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: Backups.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: I make an extra copy of every weapon I'm commissioned to make. For future reference, just in case.
No, these backups can't be ordinary weapons.
The chill you've experienced when the lids were opened just now was in no way an illusion.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: Ha! Here you are!
The ledger?

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: No, just my first works after my arrival in Eastside.
Mess withdraws a long sword from inside one of the chests. It has a hilt and scabbard that seem to be made of pure silver and are embedded with red gemstones. It looks magnificent.
But the sight of this magnificent sword turns your stomach.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: Oh, you sense the nature of this thing.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: Commissioned by an old man. He looked respectable, but acted like a Scrooge when it came time to pay.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: He planned to use this weapon to take care of his rich wife, I guess...
You knew his plan, but you didn't call the police?

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: He didn't tell me what he was going to do. It's just my guess. Call the police... what good would that have done without evidence?
Did he do it then?

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: How should I know? I haven't seen him since... Look at these two babies!
Mess picks up two terrifying one-handed morning stars.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: Made them for two scions. They wanted two identical weapons for some sort of armored combat. They acted like best buddies when they were upstairs in my living room.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: Then they came to me in private, one after the other, and each asked me to make his weapon heavier so he could destroy his opponent in combat.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: The Eastsiders are hypocrites. In Syndicate, if two persons fight, they fight fair and square.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: This one wanted to take his father out, this one wanted to get back at her ex-boyfriend, this one... I don't remember what this one wanted to do, probably not something very serious.
How...

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: Don't ask me how I know. Like I told you, I make guesses.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: Or let me put it this way... I know by looking at them.
You can read minds?

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: I'm not that good.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: I can only see malice.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: If you welcome malice into your heart, it will turn you into a puppet doing its bidding sooner or later. And the writing is on the wall for its victims.
Now you understand why you had that uncomfortable feeling when the chests were opened. It stemmed from the malice of the owners of the weapons, as Mess pointed out.
Upon hearing Mess' little speech, you have a feeling that the collective malice contained in the chests seems to have taken on a new life. It almost makes you retch.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: How are you feeling? Does it feel as if your dark side is about to break through?

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: Are you gonna do something about it? Do what people in such circumstances usually do, do something malicious...

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: ...Hey, give me some reaction. I don't just bring anybody here to look at the weapons. You're my special guest...
You didn't bring me here to look for the ledger?

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: You are so naive! This workshop is run by me and me alone. I don't need a ledger.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: I keep a copy of every piece of work. I'm sure that's good enough.
You know what your customers are going to do with the weapons, why do you still provide your services to them?!

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: You want to know why...? There are several reasons, actually.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: First and foremost, I don't care. What they want to do with the weapons is none of my concern.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: Second, most Eastsiders are chickens. They have evil thoughts, but they wouldn't dare to put them into action.
Any other reasons?

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: Other reasons? You wouldn't understand if I told you... but, er, I guess there's no harm in telling you.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: I'm fighting against a terrible, terrible thing.
What is it?

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: You're a muggle. No wonder you don't know its existence.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: This thing... it makes people do things against their will. It's the agent of all violence, the culprit for human depravity.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: Malice among mankind is its manifestation in this world. It lays waste to whatever it comes into contact with, but it is visible to no one.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: I couldn't do anything about it before. But then I became a Sinner, so I figured maybe I have a chance at it.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: My plan is to collect malevolent energies, beat this thing at its own game, and even eliminate it...

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: Each piece of work here represents each of my attempts to beat it. So far, I have had no luck. I haven't built a weapon that can hurt it.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: But that's okay. I'm making a powerful secret weapon. When it's done, I can definitely destroy this thing!
Mess is talking gibberish as if she were a lunatic. You can't get any useful information from it.
She said she doesn't have a ledger here, but she has kept a copy of every weapon she's ever made.
You said, you keep a copy of every weapon you make, right?
Find me that gas bomb, stat.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: Okay, okay, I knew you wouldn't have the patience to hear me out. I'll find you the gas bomb.
Reluctantly, Mess starts rummaging in the chests again. A short while later, she comes up with a transparent canister with liquid in it.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: Here you go! This is the one.
Tell me about this customer.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: Oh, normally I don't make gas bombs for customers. I find it distasteful.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: But this guy, he's interesting. He's one of the biggest asses among my customers, though not as big an ass as you... but big enough.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: He...
Mess' voice trails off, and she looks at you, wearing an unpleasant smile.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: I changed my mind. I don't want to tell you about him.
You have to. This is an order.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: What would you do if I refused?
Mess' provocative question drives you to the end of your patience.
With the lives of millions of Eastsiders on the line, you can't afford to let this drag on any longer.
Tell me everything about this man.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: Ahhh!

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: Cough cough... Hahaha...

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: Hahaha! Looks like you're not invincible after all... Hahaha!

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: Things have just... Hahaha... got interesting. Hahaha... You can be controlled...
Mess struggles against the power of the shackles, but fails quickly. Puffing and panting, she gives up all the information.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: Jack... Jack Naper, son of the deputy chief of... of the Eastside Public Security Bureau, a-an infamous spoiled son.
Good, continue.
Mess' breathing is steadying.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: He came to me half a year ago. Said he wanted a weapon that could create a lot of fun.
You take a look at the canister in your hand and go on questioning Mess.
What's this liquid? Why does it make people go crazy? Is there an antidote?

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: No antidote. I made it with his malice.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: You remove the safety and then pull the string, and that's it. In a few minutes, the liquid will become harmless, like water.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: Jack was happy with the product. And I haven't seen him since.
Enough.
Having attained the information you need, you turn on your communications device.
The culprit is Jack Naper, son of the deputy chief of the Eastside Public Security Bureau. Track him down immediately.
...Yes, get our people ready. We'll be right there.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: Ah, he's attacking again tonight, isn't he?
You guessed right. Or maybe, it's not a guess at all.
You turn to face Mess, and give her an order in a cold voice.
You're coming with me to stop him.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: Heh... do I get to say no?
That unpleasant smile of hers curves up the corners of her mouth once again.
